title: Pinocchio falls asleep with his feet on the pot of coals, and next morning wakes up with his feet burned away.
paragraphs: As it happened, it was a night straight out of hell. The thunder crashed and crashed, lightning flashed as if the sky were on fire, and a wild, cold wind, whistling furiously and raising an enormous cloud of dust, made all the trees in the countryside creak and groan.

Pinocchio was terribly afraid of thunder and lightning: but hunger was stronger than fear: so he pulled the door to, and setting off at a run, reached the village in a hundred leaps, with his tongue hanging out and panting like a hunting dog.
But he found everything dark and deserted. The shops were shut; the house doors shut, the windows shut, and not even a dog in the street. It seemed like a village of the dead.
Then Pinocchio, overcome by despair and hunger, grabbed a house bell and began ringing it without stopping, saying to himself:
Sure enough, an old man in a nightcap appeared and shouted angrily:
“What do you want at this hour?”
“Would you please give me a little bread?”
“Wait there, I’ll be right back,” replied the little old man, thinking he was dealing with one of those reckless boys who enjoy ringing doorbells at night to bother decent people sleeping peacefully.
Half a minute later the window opened again, and the same little old man’s voice shouted to Pinocchio:
“Come underneath and hold out your hat.”
Pinocchio, who did not yet have a hat, came closer and felt an enormous basinful of water pour down over him, watering him from head to foot as if he were a pot of drooping geraniums.

He went home as wet as a little chick and worn out with tiredness and hunger: and because he no longer had the strength to stand, he sat down, resting his soaking, muddy feet on a pot full of glowing coals.
And there he fell asleep; and as he slept, his feet, which were made of wood, caught fire and slowly, slowly burned black and turned to ash.
And Pinocchio went on sleeping and snoring, as if his feet belonged to someone else. At last, as day was breaking, he woke because someone had knocked at the door.
“Who is it?” he asked, yawning and rubbing his eyes.
